resale_co.name: Housing and Building Code Change of Occupancy & Transfer of Title (Change of Occupancy CO)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Keyport Code Enforcement Office
resale_co.lead_time: Fee depends on business days before the inspection: 10 or more business days for the lowest fee. Payment is due when the appointment is scheduled.
requirements: Application for Housing and Building Code Change of Occupancy & Transfer of Title, with owner, buyer and all occupants listed
Separate smoke detector, carbon monoxide alarm and fire extinguisher certificate from the Keyport Fire Prevention Bureau (smoke fee added to the CO fee)
Property should be vacant for the inspection; unlock the door and wait outside
GFI outlets in every bathroom and at kitchen counter outlets within six feet of a sink before a Certificate of Occupancy is issued (Code 12-12.1)
Fire extinguisher, minimum 5 lb. ABC, mounted in the kitchen (form still lists it)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Bring the completed Change of Occupancy Residential Sale application (with the Fire Prevention Bureau smoke/CO page) and payment to the Code Enforcement office at Borough Hall, 70 West Front Street. Payment is due when the appointment is scheduled. Have the house vacant and unlocked for the inspector; if it passes, the CO is left on the kitchen counter, and if not, the report is emailed.

To schedule a Change of Occupancy (CO) inspection, please bring completed paperwork
Payment must be made at the time appointment is scheduled.
If there are no code violations the inspector will leave the CO on the kitchen counter.
Change of Occupancy & Transfer of Title
BOROUGH OF KEYPORT – Code Enforcement Office

No owner shall occupy or let an occupant, nor shall any person lease or occupy, any vacant dwelling, lodging or commercial unit unless a Certificate of Occupancy, which certifies that the unit is fit for human habitation as set forth in this Code, shall first be obtained from the Code Official.

resale_co.notes: The Borough's August 2025 fillable form for a residential sale charges $110.00 / $190.00 / $245.00 plus the smoke fee, by business days. The Code (12-2.3, PM-105.12, amended by Ord. No. 1-23 in 2023, read through the ecode360 print view) still lists $75 / $155 / $210; the newer form amounts are probably current, but confirm. The form gives the Code Enforcement Office phone as 732-739-5135 (Administrative Assistant Jessi Antenucci, jantenucci@keyportonline.com). Code 12-6 (Ord. No. 21-98) also has an older $20 smoke detector inspection fee; the Fire Prevention Bureau form uses the state $45 / $90 / $161 schedule. Landlord registration is a rental-only requirement.

requirements: Smoke alarms on each level, including basements, and within 10 feet outside each sleeping area
Ten-year sealed battery single station smoke alarms listed to ANSI/UL 217; AC powered alarms from original construction may not be replaced with battery alarms
Carbon monoxide alarm within 10 feet of all sleeping areas
Minimum 5 lb. ABC fire extinguisher in the kitchen, visible, unblocked and mounted with the manufacturer's bracket (form still lists it)

fire_cert.notes: Keyport is its own fire code enforcing agency (LEA code F). The smoke/CO page is part of the Borough's August 2025 sale packet and uses the current state fee schedule ($45 / $90 / $161). The state directory lists Fire Official Anthony P Vecchio with the bureau email Firebureau@keyportonline.com; the Borough page lists Tony Vecchio, tvecchio@keyportonline.com, 732-739-5130. The form still requires a fire extinguisher, which state law (P.L.2025, c.19) dropped from the sale certificate in February 2025; confirm with the Bureau.

other_items.label: GFI outlets
other_items.detail: Every dwelling to be sold must have GFI outlets in every bathroom and at every kitchen counter outlet within six feet of a sink before a Certificate of Occupancy is issued.

other_items.label: Smoke detector inspection before transfer
other_items.detail: Code 12-6 says no one-, two- or three-family residence may be sold unless inspected and approved for smoke detectors; the Tax Collector reminds anyone ordering a tax search.

open_questions: Are the form fees ($110 / $190 / $245) current, given the Code still lists $75 / $155 / $210?
Is there a reinspection fee, and how long is the CO valid?
Does the Fire Prevention Bureau still require the fire extinguisher after P.L.2025, c.19?
